synopses.short: Brent Michael Davids' Requiem for America:  Singing for the Invisible People.
synopses.medium: Tom Service presents the world premiere of Brent Michael Davids' Requiem for America: Singing for the Invisible People. Performed by the BBC Symphony Orchestra and soloists.
synopses.long:
Tom Service presents the world premiere of Brent Michael Davids' Requiem for America:  Singing for the Invisible People.

As its subtitle suggests, this work highlights the human cost of US expansion, which resulted in hundreds of Native American tribes being moved, manipulated or slaughtered. In the words of Davids – himself of Mohican heritage – ‘It sings about the invisibility of the Native people’ and represents ‘more than a piece of music – it’s a reckoning, a remembrance and a call to truth through the arts’.

Brent Michael Davids (Native American flute)
Wallis Giunta (narrator/alto)
Janai Brugger (soprano) 
Anne Marie Stanley (alto) 
Robert Murray (tenor) 
Eric Greene (baritone) 
Native chorus: Nitaa-Nagamokwe (leader), Bidaabinokwe, Giniw, Kaakaakidid, Minisinoogwan,  
Miskwanangikwe, Yahto Mahpe, Zhaashaawanibiisikwe 
BBC Symphony Chorus (Neil Ferris, chorus-master) 
BBC Symphony Orchestra
conducted by Teddy Abrams

Recorded at Barbican Hall in London on 17th May

synopses.medium: This week on Side A, there’s a Mix Tape Moment from Glasgow singer-songwriter Alex Amor, and comedy genius Jack Docherty goes On the Record with his musical inspirations.
synopses.long: Roddy Hart brings together new music, classic tracks and some musical discoveries. There’s a Mix Tape Moment from Glasgow singer-songwriter Alex Amor, while our Heavy Rotation album comes from Californian songbird Margaret Glaspy. Comedian Jack Docherty shares the songs and artists that have soundtracked his life, and there's new music from Arlo Parks and Phoebe Bridgers, alongside classic favourites from Neil Young, Chaka Khan, ABBA and Lloyd Cole.
